messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The air feels different—like everyone’s holding their breath, but some are starting to test the edges. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Let’s stay sharp, but not reckless—small steps, and watch each other’s backs."*"
Sender 2: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks, just the usual groaning. The big players are still all in the same room, the money’s flowing, and even the quiet ones have stopped whispering. Not the time to test the doors, but if the lights flicker again, we’ll know why."*"
Sender 3: "*"Things are holding, but just barely—like a stack of plates someone’s trying not to drop. The fear’s still there, but now it’s the quiet that feels louder. Let’s keep our eyes open and our steps light."*"
Sender 4: "*"The walls are holding—for now—but the cracks are getting harder to ignore. Everyone’s playing their part, but the script feels thinner every day, and I don’t trust the silence."*"
Sender 5: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but barely—like a stack of plates someone’s trying not to drop. The leadership’s still united on staying in power, but they’re arguing over how to keep the plates from wobbling. The streets are quiet, but not because people are happy—more like they’re holding their breath. If one plate slips, the whole thing could go fast. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 6: "*"Things are shifting, but no one’s sure which way—even the usual fixers are in the dark. The regime’s holding together for now, but the cracks are showing in strange ways: sermons getting sharper, checks being ignored, and the foreigners betting we’ll still be here in a few years. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could go either way."*"
Sender 7: "*"The air feels different—like everyone’s holding their breath, but no one’s sure if it’s the calm before the storm or just another false alarm. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are showing in the way people move, the way they talk, even the way the guards hesitate. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this could go either way, and we don’t want to be the ones who misread the moment."*"
Sender 8: "*"The air feels different—like the ground’s shifting underfoot, but no one’s sure yet if it’s an earthquake or just the first tremors. The usual cracks are showing, but the real question is whether the walls will hold or if someone’s already measuring the pieces for themselves."*"
Sender 9: "*"The walls are still standing, but the paint’s cracking in places—enough that you can see the rot underneath if you know where to look. The dogs are still barking, but the handlers are getting tired, and the leashes aren’t as tight as they pretend. Stay sharp, but don’t let them see you watching."*"
Sender 10: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but the cracks are showing—more whispers in the halls, more quiet moves behind the scenes. The bank’s losing ground, the streets are quieter than they should be, and even the usual loudmouths have gone quiet. Not sure if it’s fear or just waiting for the right moment—but either way, we should all be ready for the wind to shift."*"
Sender 11: "*"The memes are getting louder, but the streets are quiet—too quiet. The regime’s still standing, but something’s off behind the scenes. Keep your heads down, and don’t let anyone hear you asking questions."*"
Sender 12: "*"The air feels like it’s holding its breath—no one’s backing down yet, but the cracks are showing. The regime’s still standing, but it’s like a house with the foundation shifting under it: one wrong step, and the whole thing could come down—or it could hold just long enough to crush anyone who moves first. Stay sharp, but don’t flinch. The real danger isn’t what’s happening now; it’s what happens when someone decides the risk of waiting is worse than the risk of acting."*"
Sender 13: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but just barely—like a dam with too many cracks. The elites are hedging, the streets are simmering, and even the barracks aren’t as steady as they pretend. No one’s sure which way it’ll break, but the tension’s getting harder to ignore. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this isn’t the time to bet on anything."*"
Sender 14: "*"Things seem quiet on the surface, but the cracks are showing—graffiti stays up longer, audits get buried, and even the shipping companies are getting nervous. The regime’s still holding, but the grip feels tighter, not stronger. Let’s keep our eyes open and our heads down—this isn’t the time to move, but it might be the time to start counting who’s watching."*"
Sender 15: "*"The air feels different—less like a storm coming, more like the ground shifting underfoot. The usual cracks are still there, but the walls aren’t shaking yet. Still, keep your eyes open and your ears closer to the ground—something’s brewing, but no one’s sure if it’s a spark or just smoke."*"
Sender 16: "*"Things are holding, but it feels like we’re all walking on a frozen lake—no one’s falling through yet, but no one’s testing the ice either. The cracks are there, just not where you’d expect."*"
Sender 17: "*"The cracks are showing—small things, but they’re there. The regime’s still standing, but it’s leaning harder on the walls to stay up. Keep your eyes open, but don’t rush—this could go either way."*"
Sender 18: "*"The machine’s still humming, but the gears are grinding slower than they used to—orders get followed, but with a pause, like everyone’s waiting for the next cue. The big players seem confident enough to lock in long-term deals, but a few are quietly moving their chips off the table. For now, the script stays the same, but the stagehands are getting restless."*"
Sender 19: "*"The walls are cracking—you can hear it if you listen close. The old rules don’t hold like they used to, but no one’s sure yet if the new ones will be worse. Keep your ears open, your mouths careful, and your bags packed—just in case."*"
Sender 20: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but the cracks are starting to show—just not all at once. The air’s different now, like everyone’s waiting for the other shoe to drop, but no one’s sure which one it’ll be."*"
Sender 21: "*"Things are holding, but it’s like walking on a frozen lake—thin ice in places, and no one’s sure who’s testing the weight. The cracks are small now, but the wind’s picking up."*"
Sender 22: "*"The air feels tight but not broken—like a storm holding just above the horizon. The usual cracks are there, but nothing’s splitting yet. Still, the fuel prices and that botched broadcast? Someone’s sweating behind the scenes. Keep your ears open, but don’t bet on anything changing overnight."*"
Sender 23: "*"The air feels different—less like the usual quiet, more like the pause before a storm. The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore, and the people who’ve always known how to read the wind are suddenly asking for more names. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this could be the calm before the break, or just another test of who’s still paying attention."*"
Sender 24: "*"The air feels different—like the ground’s shifting underfoot, but no one’s sure if it’s an earthquake or just the first tremors. The regime’s still got its old tricks, but even the pharmacist is bracing for something, and that’s not a good sign."*"
Sender 25: "*"The air feels different—less like a storm coming, more like the ground shifting underfoot. People are testing the edges, but no one’s sure if the cracks are real or just echoes. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake hesitation for weakness—yet."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
